sections.html:
Naugatuck lies in New Haven County just south of Waterbury, along the Naugatuck River, and covers 16.39 square miles. The 2020 census found 31,519 people, and the estimate for 2025 is 32,230. Median value of owner-occupied homes runs $259,100 in survey data, a figure for the borough as a whole and not a price for your house.

It is Connecticut's only consolidated town and borough, so two clerks handle official records. Ask your closing attorney which office holds the document you need. Local section names such as Union City (east of the river), Straitsville (southeast, along Route 63) and Millville (along Rubber Avenue, west side) are the labels agents and buyers use to place a house.

Rubber built this borough. Settlement dates to 1702, and Naugatuck incorporated in 1844. Nine firms joined in 1892 to form the United States Rubber Company, later Uniroyal, and the Peter Paul candy plant closed in 2007. Many neighborhoods grew up around mills that no longer run, so older construction and postponed repairs are common among sellers.

Water matters too. On August 19, 1955, rain from Hurricane Diane, more than 10 inches of it, flooded the river and changed the riverfront. If your house is near the river or a brook, ask your insurer and attorney about its flood zone status before you list. A buyer's lender will want the same answer.

sections.h2: Naugatuck property tax: what to expect
sections.html:
Real estate tax comes in two installments, due July 1 and January 1. No second bill is mailed. The top portion of the bill is the January amount and the bottom portion is the July amount, so hold on to the original. The January 2027 installment is on time through February 1, 2027.

Late payments carry 1.5 percent interest per month, and any part of a month counts as a whole one. A July installment paid in August is therefore charged 3 percent.

Tax line2025 grand list mill rate

One mill equals one dollar of tax for each $1,000 of assessed value.

  • Past-due statements for real estate go out in September and again in February.
  • Lien continuing certificates are filed in June.
  • The tax office is at 229 Church Street. The Town Hall lobby is open Monday to Thursday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.

At closing, unpaid installments, interest and liens are normally paid from your proceeds. Because interest is added monthly, ask the office for a fresh balance once you have a closing date.

sections.h2: Conveyance tax on a Naugatuck deed
sections.html:
Any deed carrying $2,000 or more in consideration is taxed, and the town clerk will not record it until the return is filed and the tax is paid. For residential property the tax has two parts.

  • State part: 0.75 percent up to $800,000, 1.25 percent from $800,000.01 to $2,500,000, and 2.25 percent above $2,500,000.
  • Municipal part: one-fourth of one percent, kept by the municipality where the deed is recorded.
  • Non-residential property other than unimproved land pays the state part at 1.25 percent.
  • A principal residence sold with a pyrrhotite concrete foundation can be exempt if an engineer certifies it. The exemption covers only the first sale after certification.

A targeted investment community may add up to another quarter of one percent. Who actually pays is a matter for your purchase contract and closing attorney.

Route 8 runs from Naugatuck to Waterbury, Derby, Torrington and Bridgeport. Route 63 leads to New Haven and Route 68 heads toward Durham. Train riders use the Naugatuck station on the Waterbury Branch of the New Haven Line.

Public schools are organized as four elementary schools (kindergarten through grade 4), two intermediate schools (grades 5 and 6), one middle school (grades 7 and 8) and Naugatuck High School. The high school finished an $81 million renovation in fall 2015.

The Naugatuck Center Historic District is on the National Register. If your house is near the Green or on Church Street, ask the borough whether any local review applies before repairs begin.

Most owners pick one of three paths: an agent listing, a sale on your own, or a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house as it stands. They trade time, cost and certainty in different amounts.

  • An agent can reach the most buyers, but showings, buyer financing, an appraisal and repair requests come with that.
  • Selling on your own saves the commission and hands you the paperwork, marketing and haggling.
  • A cash sale to a buyer like us removes lender approval and the repair list, and you pick a closing date within what the title work allows.

A cash offer reflects the condition of the house, so it can sit below a retail listing price. We cannot name a number before we review the property, and you can turn an offer down without owing anything.

In a former mill borough, the common problems are age, inheritance and timing. A house with years of deferred maintenance can be hard to finance, because a lender's appraiser may flag the roof, foundation, heating or wiring.

Inherited houses add layers. Heirs may live out of state, the title may still carry a parent's name, and the estate may need court steps before anyone can sign a deed. Back taxes grow too, since interest is added monthly and past-due notices lead to lien certificates in June.

Tenants, code questions and a mortgage that is behind round out the list. One short call to a title company or attorney will show what must be cleared before closing.

1. Send us the address, the condition and your timeline.
  2. We look over the house and check for liens, taxes or title problems.
  3. A written offer arrives, and you take as long as you need to decide.
  4. If you accept, a title company or attorney opens the file and orders the title search.
  5. The conveyance tax return goes to the town clerk, back taxes come out of proceeds, and the deed is recorded.

The tax office can quote a payoff figure, and the town clerk can confirm recording requirements. We are not a law firm, so check legal and tax questions with a Connecticut attorney or the official office.

Before closing day, collect a photo ID, your mortgage statement and the tax bill you still have. Decide what leaves with you and what stays, and empty the house of anything you are taking. A cash buyer will not ask for repairs, but a clean, cleared house makes the final walk-through quick.

faqs.q: How high is the Naugatuck mill rate?
faqs.a: The 2025 grand list rate is 40.44 for real estate and personal property and 32.46 for motor vehicles. Ask the tax office for the current figure before you estimate a payoff.

faqs.q: When are Naugatuck property taxes due?
faqs.a: July 1 and January 1. The January 2027 installment is on time if paid by February 1, 2027.

faqs.q: What interest applies to late Naugatuck taxes?
faqs.a: Late payments accrue 1.5 percent per month, with a partial month counted as a full one. A July installment paid in August is charged 3 percent.

faqs.q: Do I pay the Connecticut conveyance tax when I sell in Naugatuck?
faqs.a: The tax is imposed on the deed, and your contract and closing attorney decide who pays. Under $800,000 the residential rate is 1 percent combined, 0.75 percent state and 0.25 percent municipal.

faqs.q: Is flooding a concern in Naugatuck?
faqs.a: The river flooded on August 19, 1955, after more than 10 inches of rain from Hurricane Diane. Ask your insurer and attorney about your lot.
